title: Scenario 3 knowledge check
notes: PROVISIONAL INSTRUMENT. Revised 2026-10-28 so every item tests real farming knowledge that the game and its feedback actually teach, in plain language for smallholder farmers. Still needs supervisor review before any study use. Editing this file is enough to change the instrument - no code changes are required. Drought maize season: decide early how much ground the water can carry, share one reserve, keep committed tiles out of stress.

questions.text: In a drought, several farmers draw from the same dam or borehole. Why does a shared plan for using the water matter?
options: It does not - each farmer should take what they need while it lasts
It does not - rain will refill the dam soon enough
Every litre one person uses is gone for everyone else
So everyone can water their whole field a little each day
questions.explanation: A shared source is one supply. If everyone takes what they want, it can run dry before anyone's crop is ready. Agreeing how much land each person will water, and how much each will draw, means more crops actually reach harvest. The farm reserve in this season worked the same way.

questions.text: Halfway through a drought you only have enough water to keep about half your maize properly watered. What gives the bigger harvest?
options: Give all of the maize a little water, so none of it dies
Water whichever plants look driest each day, moving around the field
Stop watering all of it and wait for rain
Keep half properly watered and stop watering the other half
questions.explanation: Maize kept just below what it needs is stressed everywhere - it grows slowly and may not mature in time. Half a field kept properly watered usually yields more than a whole field kept thirsty. It is a hard choice, which is why it is better made early, before the water runs out.

questions.text: Some maize went dry for a long time before the rain came. It turned green again but gave a small harvest. Why?
options: Rain water is less useful to plants than tank water
Lost growth is not fully repaired - worst if it was dry around flowering
Green leaves mean it recovered, so the low harvest was just bad luck
The rain washed the fertiliser out of the soil
questions.explanation: Green leaves do not mean the crop has recovered: condition lost in a dry spell stays lost. Maize is most sensitive when the tassels and silks appear (flowering) - dryness then means poorly filled cobs, even if rain comes later. If water must be rationed, flowering is the stage to protect.
